target_customer: Mortgage lenders, who integrate Zinc into their loan systems so borrowers can buy homeowners insurance during origination
problem: Buying homeowners insurance is a slow manual step that delays mortgage closings and burdens lenders with underwriting requirements.
business_model: B2B software and insurance distribution for lenders, with carrier commissions

founders.name: Sam Li
previous_startups: Thoropass, formerly Laika (co-founder and CEO, after Zinc)
founders.background_notes: From the YC page. Education not found.

founders.name: Rafael Telahun
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder with Sam Li in a Coverager article and as founder and CEO (former) by CB Insights; both seen only as search results, not opened. The YC page lists only Sam Li.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with lenders' core loan origination systems and multiple carrier quoting systems is standard but integration heavy work.

defensibility.rationale: Deep lender integrations create switching costs once live, but lender sales cycles are long and carriers or loan platforms could build the same step.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later entrants such as Matic, Covered and Better Insurance served lenders directly; dated 2017 evidence of incumbent action was not found.

market_need_then: Lenders and borrowers faced closing delays from the insurance step; a later industry survey found 58 percent of respondents faced delays when borrowers needed more time to secure home insurance.

branding.domain_note: Used zincplatform.com, a suffix domain; it now redirects to a domain-for-sale listing

brand_strength.rationale: No brand material or press about the brand found; many unrelated companies use the name Zinc, so searches are crowded.

outcome_analysis: Zinc Platform was a 2016 New York insurtech that joined Y Combinator Winter 2017 to digitize homeowners insurance inside mortgage origination, with 11 people listed by YC. A Coverager item reported the team had shrunk to six on LinkedIn, and the domain is now for sale, but no source states why it stopped, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned. One co-founder later became CEO of Thoropass.
notes: Coverager pages returned HTTP 403 when fetched, so Coverager facts (co-founder Rafael Telahun, six employees, investor mentions) come from search result summaries only. Funding conflict: CB Insights says $0.12M seed on 2017-03-21; Persana dates it 2017-09-21; investor lists vary (Coverager summary names NEA, Highland, Index, Felicis, Foundation; another summary names Titan Partners and BoxGroup), unverified and not recorded. The $120K round rests on one database. Competitors: Matic, Covered, Blend and Better surfaced only in 2018 and later sources, so the as-of-founding list is empty. YC page and CB Insights agree on Winter 2017 and New York.
